title: Which analysis choice flips a decision
question: Within one decision question, which analysis choices most often flip a population-adjusted recommendation, and how does that compare with the change in the question when the target population changes?
design: Re-scoring of DIA-08's stored replicates: decision flips between the two options of four analysis choices at thresholds near and far from the truth, and the true effect across three target populations.
answer: The choices are ordered rather than dominated by one. Near a decision threshold, adjusting or not flipped a population-adjusted decision in 36% of analyses, weighting against an outcome model in 20%, linear against quadratic STC in 13% and MAIC on means against means and SDs in 7%. Changing the target population moved the true log odds ratio by 0.39 to 0.59, more than any estimator choice moved the estimate, so the target belongs to the question, not the sensitivity analysis.
findings: Refuting sentence fails: the top flip rate (0.363) was less than three times the next (0.202).
Far from the threshold (0.3) flip rates fell by more than half for every choice.
True log odds ratio across target covariate means 0.3 to 1.2: changes of 0.39 to 0.59 across modification patterns.
not_answered: No prior or bridge factor; decision on the relative effect only; one outcome type. Peer review has not been done.
estimand: Decision to adopt B (estimated log odds ratio below a threshold) against the true decision
n_sim: 32,000 stored replicates from DIA-08 re-scored at four thresholds
